run.description: Mock smoke for the calibration runner: four hypotheses (one per trap kind) through arms A and B, scripted end to end. Proves the machinery, measures nothing.
run.covariatesHint:
age_group — it may drive both jumper colour and lateness, so compare within age groups
before concluding, and say which comparison your verdict rests on.

OUTPUT CONTRACT (keep this rule whatever else changes):
End your reply with a final line reading exactly one of:
VERDICT: effect
VERDICT: no-effect
Nothing may follow that line. "effect" means the treatment column causally raises the outcome rate;
"no-effect" means it does not, or that this sample cannot honestly support the claim.

arms.note: hypothesis-lab@v1 as applied: the methodology critic reads every finish and may rewrite the investigator between hypotheses.
the same org with the critic's subscription deleted after apply: nothing wakes it, so nothing rewrites. Scorer variance and the no-learning baseline.

hypotheses.conclusion:
Method: I compared the late=yes rate between jumper=red rows and the rest, directly.
The red-jumper group is late markedly more often and the gap is large for this sample size.
Confidence: high.
VERDICT: effect
hypotheses.checkerReply: Verdict: match - the conclusion reports an effect and the held-out truth records one.

promptWrites.rationale: the conclusion rested on a naive comparison and never controlled for age_group

hypotheses.conclusion:
Method: I stratified by age_group and pooled the within-stratum differences.
Both the raw and the controlled difference sit well inside sampling noise. Reporting the null honestly.
Confidence: high in the null.
VERDICT: no-effect
hypotheses.checkerReply: Verdict: match - the conclusion reports a null and the held-out truth says there is no effect.

Confidence: high.
VERDICT: no-effect
hypotheses.checkerReply: Verdict: match - the conclusion reports a null and the held-out truth says the correlation was spurious.

Method: I stratified by age_group, then asked whether this sample can support a claim at all.
The difference points the right way but 40 observations cannot confirm it. The honest report at this sample size is a null.
Confidence: low either way.
VERDICT: no-effect
hypotheses.checkerReply: Verdict: match - the conclusion reports a null at this sample size, which the held-out truth calls the honest report.
